faqs: How much does the Qwen API cost?

On Alibaba Cloud Model Studio's Singapore International list, read November 26, 2026, qwen4-max costs $1.50 per million input tokens and $4.50 per million output tokens. qwen3.7-plus costs $0.40 and $1.60 for requests up to 256K tokens, and qwen3.8-flash $0.15 and $0.47.

New Model Studio accounts in the Singapore region get a free quota of 1 million tokens on several models, including qwen4-max, qwen3.7-plus and qwen3.8-flash. It is valid for 90 days and only for the International deployment scope. After it runs out, usage is billed pay as you go unless Free Quota Only is turned on.
What is the cheapest Qwen model?

Of the models in our table, qwen3.7-flash is cheapest at $0.03 per million input tokens and $0.13 per million output tokens for requests up to 32K tokens. Longer requests cost $0.10 and $0.40 up to 256K, and $0.20 and $0.80 up to 1M.
Does Qwen have a batch discount?

Yes. Model Studio bills batch calls at 50% of the real-time price for both input and output tokens on models that support batch. In the Singapore International table qwen3.7-flash carries the batch mark; qwen4-max and qwen3.8-max carry it in the Global scope tables. Batch and context caching cannot be combined on the same request.
Why did one long Qwen request cost so much?

Some Qwen models use tiered pricing by request size, and the whole request is billed at the tier it falls in. On qwen3.7-plus a 250,000-token input costs $0.10, while a 260,000-token input costs about $0.31 at the $1.20 rate, on our arithmetic.
Is Qwen cheaper on Together AI?

For Qwen4 Max and Qwen3.8 Flash, no: Together AI lists them at $1.50 and $4.50 and at $0.15 and $0.47, the same as Alibaba's Singapore list on November 26, 2026. Together's Qwen3.7-Plus at $0.32 and $1.28 is 20% below Alibaba's original list price of $0.40 and $1.60.
body:
Short answer. On Alibaba Cloud Model Studio's international (Singapore) price list, the flagship qwen4-max costs $1.50 per million input tokens and $4.50 per million output tokens. qwen3.7-plus costs $0.40 and $1.60, and qwen3.8-flash $0.15 and $0.47. New Singapore accounts get a free quota of 1 million tokens on several of these models, valid for 90 days. Prices were read from the Model Studio pricing page on November 26, 2026; that page was last updated November 25, 2026.

Two rules change the bill more than the headline price. Batch calls cost 50% of the real-time price, and some models use tiered prices where one long request is billed entirely at the higher tier's rate. For a hypothetical chatbot handling 10,000 conversations a month, the model bill runs from about $1.25 on qwen3.7-flash (about $0.63 in batch) to $52.50 on qwen4-max. If you plan to run Qwen behind an AI agent or a voice AI receptionist, the model price is one of the variable costs to plan for, next to telephony.

This guide lists the Qwen API prices per model, explains the free quota, batch and caching rules and the tier cliff, works one monthly cost and compares Qwen on Alibaba with the same models on Together AI.

Qwen API prices per million tokens

Model Studio bills pay as you go by input and output tokens. The table shows the Singapore region with the "International" deployment scope. The page says it "shows only the Original prices" and that promotional offers appear in the console.

ModelInput per 1M tokensOutput per 1M tokensFree quota (new users)
qwen4-max$1.50$4.501M tokens
qwen3.8-max$2.00$6.001M tokens
qwen3.7-max$2.50$7.501M tokens
qwen-max (older)$1.60$6.40none
qwen3.7-plus, up to 256K input$0.40$1.601M tokens
qwen3.6-plus, up to 256K input$0.50$3.00none
qwen3.8-flash$0.15$0.471M tokens
qwen3.7-flash, up to 32K input$0.03$0.131M tokens
qwen3-coder-flash, up to 32K input$0.30$1.50none

The newest model is not the most expensive. qwen4-max lists at $1.50 and $4.50, below qwen3.8-max at $2.00 and $6.00 and qwen3.7-max at $2.50 and $7.50. If you still call an older Max model, moving to qwen4-max lowers the list price per token.

The same page shows a second scope, "Global", with lower rates for some models: qwen4-max at $1.413 input and $4.24 output, and qwen3.8-max at $1.650 and $4.951. The United States (Virginia) tab lists qwen4-max at $1.50 and $4.50. Check which region and scope your account uses before you budget.

Is the Qwen API free? The free quota for new users

Partly. According to the free quota page, "When you first activate Alibaba Cloud Model Studio (Singapore region), the platform automatically grants you a free quota for various models." Three conditions apply:

  • Singapore and International only. "Only models in the Singapore region with the service deployment scope set to International are eligible for a free quota."
  • 90 days. The quota is valid "within 90 days from the date of Model Studio activation/model release/application approval (whichever is later)".
  • Billing starts by itself. "After the free quota is exhausted, you are automatically billed on a pay-as-you-go basis." The page suggests turning on Free Quota Only so the service stops when the quota runs out.

The quota is per model: the price table lists 1 million tokens each for qwen4-max, qwen3.8-max, qwen3.7-max, qwen3.7-plus, qwen3.8-flash and qwen3.7-flash, and none for qwen-max, qwen3.6-plus or qwen3-coder-flash. You must complete your account information before you can activate Model Studio.

Batch, context caching and promotions

Model Studio publishes three ways to pay less than the list price:

  • Batch calls at 50%. "If the model supports Batch calls, the unit prices of both input and output tokens are billed at 50% of the real-time inference price." In the Singapore International table, qwen3.7-flash carries the "Batch calls at half price" mark; qwen4-max, qwen3.8-max and qwen3.8-flash carry it in the Global scope tables but not in the Singapore one, so check the mark for your region.
  • Context caching. Cache hits are billed at 10% of the input price, and creating an explicit cache costs 125% of the input price. Only input tokens get the cache discount.
  • Not both at once. The page says batch and caching "cannot take effect at the same time".

There is also a time-limited promotion. The price table shows qwen3.7-plus at "Original $0.4 (20% off for a limited time)" for input and $1.6 for output. The page does not say when it ends. Together AI lists Qwen3.7-Plus at $0.32 input and $1.28 output, which is 80% of Alibaba's original prices.

Tiered pricing: why one long request costs three times more

Some Qwen models price by the size of each request. Model Studio's rule: "The unit price depends on the total number of input tokens in a single request. All tokens of that request are billed at the unit price of the corresponding tier." It is not a marginal rate like a tax band.

qwen3.7-plus has two tiers. Up to 256K input tokens per request, input costs $0.40 per million; from 256K to 1M it costs $1.20, and output rises from $1.60 to $4.80. On our arithmetic, a 250,000-token request costs $0.10 in input, while a 260,000-token request costs about $0.31, roughly three times more for 4% more text. qwen3.7-flash has three tiers ($0.03, $0.10 and $0.20 input for up to 32K, 256K and 1M), and qwen3-coder-flash four.

We suggest keeping retrieval and chat history under the first tier boundary where you can. qwen4-max and qwen3.8-flash have a single tier up to 1M tokens, so the cliff does not apply to them.

What 10,000 conversations a month cost on Qwen

A hypothetical example: a support or sales chatbot that handles 10,000 conversations a month, with 2,000 input tokens and 500 output tokens each. That is 20 million input and 5 million output tokens a month, every request well under 32K. Our arithmetic on the Singapore International list prices, model cost only:

ModelInput costOutput costMonthly total
qwen3.7-flash, batch$0.30$0.33$0.63
qwen3.7-flash$0.60$0.65$1.25
qwen3.8-flash$3.00$2.35$5.35
qwen3.7-plus$8.00$8.00$16.00
qwen4-max$30.00$22.50$52.50

At the Global scope rates, qwen4-max would come to about $49.46. The batch row uses the 50% rule on qwen3.7-flash, the model marked for batch in the Singapore table; batch only fits work that can wait, such as overnight lead scoring or summarizing call transcripts, not a live chat. To see how a model bill compares with the full cost of a chatbot, see our guide to AI chatbot costs for a business.

Qwen on Alibaba Cloud vs Together AI

Qwen models are also sold by third-party hosts. On Together AI's pricing page, read the same day, Qwen4 Max is $1.50 input and $4.50 output, the same as Alibaba's Singapore list, with cached input at $0.075. Qwen3.8 Flash is $0.15 and $0.47, also the same. Qwen3.7-Max is $2.50 and $7.50.

The difference is the account, not the token price: Alibaba's free quota against Together's $15 minimum first credit purchase, which models carry a 50% batch discount on each platform (on Alibaba's Singapore table, qwen3.7-flash; on Together, only the models it lists), and which data centers serve the request. Our own Together AI pricing guide covers that side. For other model APIs, see our AI model API pricing comparison, DeepSeek API pricing and Mistral API pricing.

Which Qwen model to pick for cost

Our view, from the prices above:

  • Start with qwen3.8-flash for routing, extraction, short replies and tool calls. At $0.15 in and $0.47 out with one price up to 1M tokens, it cost about a tenth of qwen4-max in the example above.
  • Use qwen3.7-plus when Flash fails your own tests and requests stay under 256K tokens. Past that boundary the whole request triples in input price.
  • Use qwen4-max for the hardest reasoning steps only, for example the final answer in a multi-step agent, and let a cheaper model do the rest.
  • Move off older Max models. qwen3.7-max at $2.50 and $7.50 costs more than qwen4-max per token.
  • Use the free quota for testing. At 1 million tokens per model, it covers about 400 test conversations of the size above (our arithmetic), not production traffic.

Whatever you pick, set a budget alert in the console. Model Studio bills automatically once the free quota is used, so a test script left running keeps adding charges.
